items.title: Ember’s new temperature-controlled mug makes my nightly tea ritual even better
items.author: Lauren Forristal
items.content: <article>The biggest change about Ember's new mug is that you no longer have to open the app to adjust your drink’s temperature.</article>

items.title: Mark Wahlberg wants to take on the longevity-startup crowd with an affordable gym concept
items.author: Connie Loizos
items.content:
<article>Mark Wahlberg, who once sank money into a gym chain that got kicked off the NYSE, is now building his own, and he promises you’ll get a cold plunge, a blood panel and a protein muffin without needing a trust fund.
</article>

items.title: Replit is no longer working with Anthropic, CEO says
items.author: Lucas Ropek
items.content: <article>Masad said the decision was made for a number of different reasons, including cost. Replit announced a partnership with OpenAI in August, but there was never any indication that it was no longer with Anthropic.</article>

items.title: Porsche’s electric Macan Turbo is an automotive existential crisis
items.author: Tim De Chant
items.content: <article>The 2026 Porsche Macan Turbo EV is a two-row crossover with 630 horsepower and a 100-kilowatt-hour battery. </article>

items.title: India becomes the latest country to report rogue AI agent activity
items.author: Aditya Mehta
items.content: <article>The agents got in through credentials and connection settings left exposed in app configurations, public code repositories, and overly permissive cloud roles.</article>

items.title: An Nvidia insider-turned-VC on why robotics hasn’t hit its ChatGPT moment, yet
items.author: Theresa Loconsolo
items.content: <article>Amulya Vishwanath, who spent seven years leading product marketing for NVIDIA’s robotics platforms, says robotics is currently in its “Lego era,” with the basic building blocks like actuators, robotic hands, software, and safety standards still being rebuilt.  This view runs counter to those who believe that robotics, powered by a general foundation model, is about to have […]</article>

items.title: Waymo’s robotaxis are headed to Canada
items.author: Kirsten Korosec
items.content: <article>The company will start off by testing its self-driving vehicles on Toronto's streets.</article>

items.title: Elorian’s first AI model wants to reason with images, not just about them
items.author: Aditya Mehta
items.content: <article>According to Elorian's evaluations, Glimpse outperforms even GPT-6 Astra on scientific chart reasoning and short-form video captioning, with competitive results on other visual reasoning tasks. </article>

items.title: In ‘You Can See Everything,’ Elizabeth Holmes meets her equal in comedian Nathan Fielder
items.author: Amanda Silberling
items.content: <article>Nathan Fielder's documentary about disgraced Theranos CEO Elizabeth Holmes has created a constellation of colliding personas that interrogate the very nature of authenticity.</article>

items.title: Tressfecta wants to make hair braiding a less arduous task for hairstylists
items.author: Dominic-Madori Davis
items.content: <article>Tressfecta builds products for textured hair. Its first project is a tool called Plait Pilot that helps braiders with the initial process of separating hair from packs before braiding begins. </article>

items.title: Jev is Vercel’s fastest-adopted AI model ever
items.author: Russell Brandom
items.content: <article>The data comes from Vercel's AI gateway, a unified API service similar to OpenRouter.</article>

items.title: Mark Wahlberg on using AI in film ‘the right way’ and being open to an AI clone carrying on his legacy
items.author: Aisha Malik
items.content: <article>Actor and angel investor Mark Wahlberg says he's OK with using AI in filmmaking, provided it's used "to enhance what you're doing." </article>

items.title: Veritas expands its anti-counterfeit chip to jewelry, trophies, and fragrance bottles
items.author: Ivan Mehta
items.content: <article>Counterfeiters are getting better at replicating brands' marks and passing off dupes, known as "superfakes," as genuine items. A startup called Veritas wants to tackle the problem with its own chip that verifies goods.</article>

items.title: Replit’s CEO says the future of work is the ‘self-driving company’
items.author: Sarah Perez
items.content: <article>Replit CEO Amjad Masad envisions a future of “self-driving companies,” where AI agents handle day-to-day tasks and people focus on higher-level decisions.</article>

items.title: Even Benchmark thinks AI is eroding the venture pact against backing rivals
items.author: Connie Loizos
items.content: <article>Benchmark says the Valley’s rule against backing rivals is getting harder to keep.</article>

items.title: Tesla reveals SpaceX-powered Roadster that flies and falls with style
items.author: Sean O'Kane
items.content: <article>The new car used thrusters to leap over a Cybercab, Cybertruck, Tesla Semi, Model Y, and Model 3 at a demo in Texas.</article>

items.title: When it came to Cal AI’s viral success, a small army of influencers paid off
items.author: Lucas Ropek
items.content: <article>The company generated over $30 million in revenue in two years and was acquired by MyFitnessPal for an undisclosed amount of money in March.</article>

items.title: And the winner of Startup Battlefield at Disrupt 2026 is: Intero Biosystems
items.author: Sean O'Kane
items.content: <article>Intero Biosystems beat out 199 other Startup Battlefield companies to take home the $100,000 grand prize at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026.</article>

items.title: Amazon devices chief Panos Panay on the importance of failure and bouncing back from it
items.author: Aisha Malik
items.content: <article>Panay said that it's possible to recover and learn from all sorts of failures, even catastrophic ones, when building products. </article>

items.title: Meta launches an open-weight AI model that runs on Macs
items.author: Lucas Ropek
items.content: <article>Meta and Apple have teamed up for the launch of the social media giant's newest model, Muse Spark Open, which will run locally on Apple silicon. </article>
